Task guide

Setting up account assignment

Where Odoo takes the account for every line of a document, and how to set up product categories, products, fiscal positions, taxes, partners and default accounts so that invoices are posted correctly without anyone touching them.

CountrySlovakia
EditionOdoo Community
Coversaccount, product, l10n_sk, sale_order_advance_invoice, l10n_sk_sale_order_advance_invoice, purchase_order_advance_invoice, l10n_sk_purchase_order_advance_invoice, l10n_sk_account_cutoff

What this guide is for

In Odoo nobody assigns accounts to an invoice by hand (the predkontácia of Slovak practice): every line gets its account from rules set once — on the product, the product category, the tax, the partner and the company settings. Set up well, whoever issues invoices never sees an account and the accountant re-posts nothing. Set up badly, everything lands on the default accounts.

The guide is for the Accountant role and belongs at the start, before the first invoice. How the individual documents are posted is shown in Daily bookkeeping.

Where the account comes from

Line of the document Odoo takes the first one that is set
Invoice line with a product Income Account / Expense Account on the product → on its category (or a parent category) → Product Accounts in the company settings
Invoice line without a product the account used most often with this partner on this kind of document → the journal's Default Account
Receivable, payable the partner's Account Receivable / Account Payable
VAT the account on the tax (its distribution lines)
Payment, bank statement the bank journal's accounts and the company settings

After that, the document's fiscal position can still swap taxes and accounts (Account Mapping).

What is set after installation

Odoo's Slovak chart of accounts sets 604000 Sales of goods and 504000 Goods sold for every product and every category — in Accounting → Configuration → Settings, block Default Accounts, line Product Accounts, and on every existing product category as well. The sales journal's Default Account is 604000, the purchase journal's 504000.

Without further setup, revenue from services therefore goes to 604 instead of 602, and purchased services, energy or material to 504 instead of 518, 502 or 501.

Product categories

The category is what a Slovak accountant knows as the predkontácia: the kind of supply decides the account. Accounting → Configuration → Invoicing → Product Categories, on each category the Income Account and Expense Account fields.

An example split (for inventory accounted by method B):

Category Income Account Expense Account
Goods 604000 Sales of goods 504000 Goods sold
Own products 601000 Sales of own products —
Services 602000 Revenue from the sale of services 518000 Other services
Material — 501000 Material consumption
Energy — 502000 Energy consumption
Repairs and maintenance — 511000 Repair and maintenance
Travel — 512000 Travel
Representation — 513000 Representation costs

Refine the accounts with sub-accounts from your own chart (518100 Rent, 518200 Telephones…) and categories for them. Categories can have sub-categories; a sub-category without an account inherits its parent's.

Under method A, purchased goods and material are posted to 131 / 111 and reach expenses when issued from stock. That is set up by the module l10n_sk_stock_account_method_a, shipped separately. Fixed assets are posted to 042 through the asset profile — a separate guide will cover them.

Products

On a product (Accounting → Customers → Products or Vendors → Products) the account comes from its Product Category; the Accounting tab lets one product use a different Income Account or Expense Account. Keep exceptions on the product for real exceptions — the rule belongs on the category, or the assignment falls apart into hundreds of products.

For recurring costs without stock — rent, electricity, telephone, the accountant's fee — it pays to create a product of type Service in the right category. On the bill you pick the product, and the account and tax are right straight away.

A line without a product gets the account used most often with the same partner. That helps with a vendor who always invoices the same thing, but the first bill of a new vendor falls to the purchase journal's Default Account (504000). You can change that account in Accounting → Configuration → Accounting → Journals to whichever is most common for you.

Fiscal positions

A fiscal position is the tax regime of trading with a partner. A product carries its taxes and accounts as they apply at home; the fiscal position swaps them on a particular document according to whom you trade with. A customer in another EU country with a VAT number is thus invoiced an exempt supply instead of 23 %, and VAT on a bill from an EU supplier is self-assessed — all from one product with one set of taxes, without whoever issues the invoice having to pick the right tax every time.

How it is applied:

  1. The document has a Fiscal Position field (tab Other Info). It is filled from the partner when you choose the partner on the document; on a draft you can change it and the taxes on the lines are recomputed.
  2. The partner either has it set by hand — the Fiscal Position field on the Sales & Purchase tab — or Odoo finds it: a position with Detect Automatically ticked applies to partners from the country or Country Group in its settings, optionally only to those with a VAT number (VAT required). The first that matches, in the order of the list, is used.
  3. The position swaps taxes (each of its taxes says which taxes it replaces) and optionally accounts (Account Mapping).

The Slovak chart has four positions, all detected automatically (Accounting → Configuration → Accounting → Fiscal Positions):

Fiscal position For a partner What it swaps
Domestic (Obchody v SK) from Slovakia taxes stay domestic; the general sales tax 23% becomes the goods variant 23% T
Eu intra (Obchody s EU) from the EU with a VAT number sales: 0% EÚ T (supply of goods) or 0% EÚ S (service), both for the EC sales list; purchases: 23 % EÚ (acquisition of goods) or 23 % EÚ S (service received), self-assessed
Eu private (Obchody s EU konzument) from the EU without a VAT number taxes stay domestic — sold with Slovak VAT
Export Outside EU (Vývoz mimo EU) from anywhere else sales: 0 % VÝV (export)

A partner without a country gets no position at all, and the document carries the product's taxes unchanged — so always fill in the partner's country.

Which variant the position picks depends on the tax on the product — which is why services must carry 23% S: Taxes on the product. On an import of goods the VAT is paid to customs, not to the supplier: l10n_sk_jcd.

Domestic reverse charge (§ 69(12)) is not handled by a fiscal position in the Slovak chart: it depends not on the partner but on the kind of supply — construction work, metals, mobile phones and others. Give such products the reverse-charge taxes directly: Sales Taxes 0 % Prenos daňovej povinnosti (§69 ods. 12, A.2), Purchase Taxes 23 % PREN (or 19 % or 5 %). If you trade with a partner only under this regime, a construction subcontractor for example, you can create a fiscal position of your own without Detect Automatically that swaps the domestic taxes for the reverse-charge ones, and assign it to that partner by hand.

The Slovak positions change taxes only, not accounts: revenue from an EU customer goes to the same 604 or 602 as domestic revenue. To keep EU and export revenue on sub-accounts of their own, add an Account Mapping to the position: Account on Product 604000, Account to Use Instead for example 604100.

Taxes on the product

Taxes do not belong on the category but on the product: the Sales Taxes and Purchase Taxes fields on the General Information tab. The Slovak taxes come in two variants for each rate, and the difference only shows when trading abroad:

Tax For Domestic With a customer or vendor from the EU
23% (sales) goods becomes 23% T 0% EÚ T — supply of goods to the EU
23% S (sales) services stays 0% EÚ S — service to the EU
23% (purchases) goods stays 23 % EÚ — acquisition of goods from the EU
23% S (purchases) services stays 23 % EÚ S — service received from the EU (§ 69(3))

The same holds for the 19 % and 5 % rates. The swap is done by the fiscal position — Domestic, Eu intra, Export Outside EU — which a partner gets automatically from its country and VAT number.

A new product gets its taxes from the Default Taxes block in the settings (23% for sales and purchases), so the goods variant even for a service. For services change them to 23% S, or a service from the EU is reported as an acquisition of goods, and a service to the EU as a supply of goods in the EC sales list.

The VAT accounts sit on the tax and need no changing:

Account Tax
343220 VAT base sales rate output VAT 23 %
343210 VAT lower sales rate output VAT 19 % and 5 %
343120 VAT base purchase rate input VAT 23 %
343110 VAT lower purchase rate input VAT 19 % and 5 %
548000 Other costs of economic activity the non-deductible half of VAT on a vehicle with 50 % deduction

With a reverse charge and an acquisition from the EU, the VAT is posted to both sides of the same 343 account.

Partners: receivables and payables

On the partner, tab Invoicing, the Account Receivable (by default 311000 Receivables) and Account Payable (321000 Suppliers) fields. Change them for partners whose balances you keep separately — related parties, employees, shareholders. Only an account of type Receivable or Payable can be chosen, and in the Slovak chart that is 311 and 321 and a few others (378000 Other receivables). For the rest, create a sub-account of that type in the chart of accounts, for example 311100 Receivables – related parties.

The company's default accounts

Accounting → Configuration → Settings, block Default Accounts:

Setting Default For
Exchange difference entries: Gain / Loss 663000 / 563000 realised exchange differences on payment
Bank transactions and payments: Bank Suspense 261000 Money in transit a statement line not yet matched
Internal Transfer 261001 Liquidity Transfer transfers between your own bank accounts
Early payment discounts 646000 / 546000 cash discounts from payment terms — do not use them in Slovakia, see below
Product Accounts 604000 / 504000 the last resort when neither the product nor its category has an account

A cash discount (skonto) for early payment is always settled by a credit note in Slovakia, because changing the VAT already declared needs a document. Odoo's payment terms do offer an Early Discount, but it posts the discount at payment and reduces the VAT with no document at all. Leave it off on the payment terms; when a customer pays early with the discount, issue a credit note for the discount amount (Daily bookkeeping).

The exception is a discount from a foreign supplier: no credit note will come from them, and when you pay their bill early with the discount, the difference is posted to 648000 Other income from economic activities. In the Pay window enter the reduced amount, set Payment Difference to Mark as fully paid and the Difference Account to 648000.

Payments registered by hand (the Pay button) go through 221002 Outstanding Receipts and 221003 Outstanding Payments until a bank statement matches them. The bank journal has Default Account 221001 and Suspense Account 261000; for every new bank account, check that it has a 221 sub-account of its own.

The localization sets further accounts itself when it is installed; this is where to find them in the settings:

Where in Settings Accounts Set by
Sales, block Invoicing 324001 advance clearing, 324000 short-term, 475000 long-term advances received l10n_sk_sale_order_advance_invoice
Accounting, block Received Advance Invoices 314001 clearing, 314000 advances granted l10n_sk_purchase_order_advance_invoice
Accounting, block Cut-offs 381000, 383000, 384000, 385000 l10n_sk_account_cutoff

Account 385000 has a wrong Slovak name in Odoo's Slovak chart, Náklady budúcich období (krátkodobé) (deferred charges); it is Príjmy budúcich období (accrued income). Until the name is corrected, rename it in the chart of accounts.

Checking the assignment

  1. Before confirming an invoice, open the Journal Items tab: in draft it shows exactly the lines that will be posted.
  2. After the first month, open Accounting → Review → Control → Journal Items, group by Account and then Product. A service on 604000 or an energy bill on 504000 stands out at a glance.
  3. Reset a wrongly posted invoice in an open period with Reset to Draft, correct the product or account, and confirm again. Correct the category or product as well, so the mistake does not repeat.
